amharic.name: አማርኛ ፊደል (Amharic Fidel)
amharic.description: Amharic uses the Ge'ez script (Fidel), an abugida where each character represents a consonant+vowel combination. Below are the base consonants with the 'ä' vowel.

tigrinya.name: ትግርኛ ፊደል (Tigrinya Fidel)
tigrinya.description: Tigrinya uses the Ge'ez script like Amharic. Below are the base consonants.

arabic.name: الأبجدية العربية (Arabic Alphabet)
arabic.description: Arabic is written right-to-left. Letters change form based on position in the word.

russian.name: Русский Алфавит (Russian Alphabet)
russian.description: Russian uses the Cyrillic script with 33 letters.

chinese_pinyin.name: 汉语拼音 (Chinese Pinyin)
chinese_pinyin.description: Pinyin is the romanization system for Standard Chinese. Below are the initials and finals.

japanese_hiragana.name: ひらがな (Japanese Hiragana)
japanese_hiragana.description: Hiragana is a Japanese syllabary with 46 basic characters. Each represents a syllable (consonant + vowel).
japanese_hiragana.special_notes: Hiragana has 46 basic characters. Dakuten (゛) changes voicing. Handakuten (゜) changes to P sound.

korean_hangul.name: 한글 (Korean Hangul)
korean_hangul.description: Hangul is a Korean alphabet with 14 consonants and 10 vowels. Letters combine into syllable blocks.
korean_hangul.special_notes: Created by King Sejong in 1443. Letters combine into syllable blocks (consonant + vowel + optional final consonant).

italian.name: Alfabeto Italiano
italian.description: Italian alphabet has only 21 letters (J, K, W, X, Y used only in foreign words). Double consonants are important.
italian.special_notes: H is silent. Rolled R. Double consonants are pronounced longer. C before E/I sounds like 'ch'.

portuguese.name: Alfabeto Português
portuguese.description: Portuguese uses the Latin alphabet with nasal vowels and cedilla (Ç).
portuguese.special_notes: Nasal vowels (ã, õ). Ç used before A, O, U. X has multiple pronunciations. Accents: á, â, à, é, ê, í, ó, ô, ú.

greek.name: Ελληνικό αλφάβητο (Greek Alphabet)
greek.description: The Greek alphabet has 24 letters and is the ancestor of Latin and Cyrillic scripts.
greek.special_notes: Origin of many scientific symbols. Uppercase and lowercase forms. Γ sounds like 'y' before certain vowels.

hebrew.name: אלפבית עברי (Hebrew Alphabet)
hebrew.description: Hebrew has 22 consonant letters. It's written right to left. Vowels are indicated by niqqud (dots).
hebrew.special_notes: Written right to left. Some letters have final forms (כ→ך, מ→ם, נ→ן, פ→ף, צ→ץ). Vowels shown with dots.

hindi.name: हिंदी वर्णमाला (Hindi Alphabet)
hindi.description: Hindi uses Devanagari script with 13 vowels and 33 consonants. Written left to right.
hindi.special_notes: Consonants have inherent 'a' sound. Matras (vowel signs) modify consonants. Halant (्) removes inherent vowel.

thai.name: อักษรไทย (Thai Alphabet)
thai.description: Thai has 44 consonants and 32 vowels. It's a tonal language with 5 tones.
thai.special_notes: 5 tones: mid, low, falling, high, rising. No spaces between words. Vowels can appear before, after, above, or below consonants.

vietnamese.name: Bảng chữ cái tiếng Việt (Vietnamese Alphabet)
vietnamese.description: Vietnamese uses Latin alphabet with 29 letters and 6 tones marked by diacritics.
vietnamese.special_notes: 6 tones marked with diacritics. Đ is unique. Many vowel variations with diacritics.

turkish.name: Türk Alfabesi (Turkish Alphabet)
turkish.description: Turkish uses Latin alphabet with 29 letters. Has vowel harmony and special characters.
turkish.special_notes: Vowel harmony rule. I and İ are different letters. Ğ is usually silent or lengthens previous vowel. C sounds like 'j'.

swedish.name: Svenska Alfabetet (Swedish Alphabet)
swedish.description: Swedish has 29 letters including Å, Ä, Ö. Has pitch accent.
swedish.special_notes: Pitch accent important. Long and short vowel distinction. Å, Ä, Ö come at end of alphabet.

dutch.name: Nederlands Alfabet (Dutch Alphabet)
dutch.description: Dutch uses Latin alphabet with 26 letters. Known for its guttural G sound.
dutch.special_notes: Guttural G sound. IJ sometimes considered single letter. Diphthongs: ij, ei, ou, au, ui, oe.

oromo.name: Qubee (Oromo Alphabet)
oromo.description: Oromo uses Latin script called Qubee. Spoken primarily in Ethiopia.
oromo.special_notes: Oromo uses Latin script called Qubee. 5 vowel system. C, V, X, Z used mainly in borrowed words.

somali.name: Af Soomaali (Somali Alphabet)
somali.description: Somali uses Latin script. Spoken in Somalia, Ethiopia, Djibouti, and Kenya.
somali.special_notes: C represents pharyngeal sound. No P, V in native words. 5 vowel system.

hadiyaa.name: Hadiyyisa (Hadiyya Alphabet)
hadiyaa.description: Hadiyya uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
hadiyaa.special_notes: Abugida system where each character represents consonant+vowel. 7 vowel orders per consonant.

wolayitta.name: Wolaytta Alphabet
wolayitta.description: Wolaytta uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
wolayitta.special_notes: Also spelled Wolaita/Wolyitta. Abugida system with 7 vowel orders. Used in SNNPR region of Ethiopia.

afar.name: Qafar Alphabet
afar.description: Afar uses Latin script. Spoken in Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti.
afar.special_notes: Cushitic language. Known for guttural sounds. Latin script adopted in 1970s.

gamo.name: Gamo Alphabet
gamo.description: Gamo uses Ethiopic (Ge'ez) script. Spoken in southern Ethiopia.
gamo.special_notes: Omotic language. Abugida system with 7 vowel orders per consonant.

swahili.name: Kiswahili Alphabet
swahili.description: Swahili uses Latin script. Lingua franca of East Africa.
swahili.special_notes: Bantu language with Arabic influence. 5 vowel system. No Q, X in native words.

kinyarwanda.name: Ikinyarwanda Alphabet
kinyarwanda.description: Kinyarwanda uses Latin script. Official language of Rwanda.
kinyarwanda.special_notes: Bantu language. 5 vowel system. Tonal language with high and low tones.

kirundi.name: Ikirundi Alphabet
kirundi.description: Kirundi uses Latin script. Official language of Burundi.
kirundi.special_notes: Bantu language closely related to Kinyarwanda. 5 vowel system. Tonal language.

luo.name: Dholuo Alphabet
luo.description: Luo uses Latin script. Spoken in Kenya and Tanzania.
luo.special_notes: Nilotic language. Tonal with 4 tones. No F, Q, V, X, Z in native words.

luganda.name: Oluganda Alphabet
luganda.description: Luganda uses Latin script. Spoken in Uganda.
luganda.special_notes: Bantu language. Double consonants indicate gemination. Tonal language.

dinka.name: Thuɔŋjäŋ Alphabet
dinka.description: Dinka uses Latin script. Spoken in South Sudan.
dinka.special_notes: Nilotic language. Highly tonal with 4 tones. Uses special vowels: ɛ, ɔ, ä, ë, ï, ö.

nuer.name: Thok Naath Alphabet
nuer.description: Nuer uses Latin script. Spoken in South Sudan and Ethiopia.
nuer.special_notes: Nilotic language related to Dinka. Highly tonal. Uses special vowels: ɛ, ɔ, ä, ë, ï, ö.

bengali.name: বাংলা বর্ণমালা (Bengali Alphabet)
bengali.description: Bengali uses its own script. Spoken in Bangladesh and West Bengal, India.
bengali.special_notes: Abugida script with 11 vowels and 39 consonants. Inherent vowel 'ô'. Conjunct consonants common.

telugu.name: తెలుగు లిపి (Telugu Script)
telugu.description: Telugu uses its own script. Spoken in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, India.
telugu.special_notes: Abugida script with 16 vowels and 36 consonants. Known for rounded shapes. Called 'Italian of the East'.

kurdish.name: Alfabêya Kurdî (Kurdish Alphabet)
kurdish.description: Kurdish uses Latin (Kurmanji) or Arabic (Sorani) script. Spoken in Kurdistan region.
kurdish.special_notes: Kurmanji uses Latin script with special letters: Ç, Ê, Î, Ş, Û. Sorani uses modified Arabic script.

farsi.name: الفبای فارسی (Persian Alphabet)
farsi.description: Persian/Farsi uses modified Arabic script. Spoken in Iran, Afghanistan, Tajikistan.
farsi.special_notes: Persian uses modified Arabic script with 4 extra letters (پ, چ, ژ, گ). Written right to left. Short vowels usually not written.
